title: Chiyalik culture
fact_summary: An archaeological culture of the 11th to 14th centuries in the Volga-Ural region. Some researchers think it was left by Hungarians who stayed in the East.

claims.text: A 2022 study lists the Gulyukovo, Novo Hozyatovo and Gornovo cemeteries as belonging to the Chiyalik culture and dates it to the 11th–14th centuries.

The study reports genetic connections between the earlier Bolshie Tigani population and later Chiyalik sites, and dates the split between the ancestors of the Chiyalik group and the conquering Hungarians to the ninth century.
claims.certainty_reason: This records what the study reports, read in the open copy linked under Sources.

claims.text: Chiyalik communities “may have been later communities of the Hungarians who remained in the East”.
claims.certainty_reason: The authors themselves word it as a possibility.

claims.text: Part of the Chiyalik population “was most probably assimilated into the Bashkirs during the Middle Ages”.

open_questions.text: Is a shared genetic line enough to say that the Chiyalik people spoke Hungarian?
